newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Floods to reduce Czech tax take - agency.
newsitem.headline: Floods to reduce Czech tax take - agency.

text.p: Recent floods in the Czech Republic will likely mean that taxes collected by the state will be more than 10 billion crown lower than expectations, the CTK news agency quoted Finance Minister Ivan Pilip as saying on Monday.

The minister said the floods, which have devastated low-lying areas in the east the past two weeks, were cutting the chances of keeping the state budget in balance this year as taxes from afflicted companies would slump.

"The room of the government to take some steps to (the budget's) balance is very limited at this moment," Pilip told CTK. The types of taxes and the budget period Pilip was referring to were not made clear.
The minister rejected suggestions that state finances would slip into deficit next year. "The budget for 1998 will be planned as at least balanced," he said.
The central bank has called for a surplus budget in 1997 and 1998 to slow down demand which is contributing to the country's growing current account deficit.
Trade and current account deficits triggered a run on the crown which forced the central bank to float the currency in May.
After the crown was floated the government adopted a second series of budget cuts in as many months to compensate for a slowdown in budget revenues, while reducing demand.
The government and the parliament have approved the issuing of up to five billion in flood bonds, and released some six billion in other funds to help the flooded areas.
